scope: Original 1994 SNES DKC1; later-game and later-studio material is explicitly bounded.
evidence_policy: Primary interviews and developer statements support production history; manufacturer documents explain mechanisms. Historical evidence does not accept a patch or performance.

sources.title: Rare Scribes December 21 2005
sources.author: Rare staff reply relaying a list supplied by David Wise
sources.locator: Question from Jean-Marc Goulet about individual DKC song credits; Rare Reply beginning “Let’s see”
sources.supports: Track attribution: seven named Novakovic pieces, Funky’s Fugue by Beanland, remaining tracks by Wise.
sources.limits: Retrospective developer list, not original session files or an instrument inventory. Archive timestamp is December 27, distinct from publication.

sources.title: David Wise Interview Revisiting Donkey Kong Country
sources.author: Chris Greening interviewing David Wise
sources.locator: Questions on first-game influences and the experimental DKC2 approach; answers explicitly returning to DKC1 Aquatic Ambience
sources.supports: Three jungle demos combined into DK Swing; film/rock/dance influences; Wavestation-inspired waveform sequencing for Aquatic Ambience.
sources.limits: Later Roland Juno-2 sampling discussion is explicitly DKC2. No exact DKC1 pad preset is identified. Retrieved page does not display publication date.

sources.title: Interview David Wise page 2
sources.author: Lewis Hampson interviewing David Wise
sources.locator: Questions on dynamic/varied atmosphere and Aquatic Ambience
sources.supports: Eight-note resource limit helped integrate ambience into music; Aquatic Ambience took five weeks, mainly technical experimentation with short waveforms.
sources.limits: Composer recollection explains method and intent, not a complete source-sample list.

sources.title: Donkey Kong Country’s David Wise Talks Legacy Nintendo Switch and More
sources.author: Marc Deschamps interviewing David Wise
sources.locator: Naturally integrated compositions; Ambient sounds influence ambient music; No midi for the SNES
sources.supports: Music entered development early; environmental sounds were planned rhythmically; coded SNES music and repeated detail revision.
sources.limits: Reported 64K/eight-channel limits are a composer’s production summary, not a RAM allocation specification. Does not establish every fan MIDI as wrong.

sources.title: The Tale of Rare’s Unsung Virtuoso And Voice Of Perfect Dark Eveline Novakovic
sources.author: L.D. Murphy interviewing Eveline Novakovic
sources.locator: Early background through the first DKC project; paragraphs about quantifying notes/envelopes and working directly on SNES
sources.supports: Film-score background; manual pitch/duration/envelope/volume work; shift from keyboard notation to direct SNES composition.
sources.limits: Some credit descriptions are author narrative; Rare archive supplies the broader credit list. Later Winning Run and DKC3 details are not DKC1 production facts.

sources.title: Month Of Kong The Making Of Donkey Kong Country
sources.author: Damien McFerran interviewing David Wise and Brendan Gunn
sources.locator: Soundtrack discussion beginning with Wise expecting a Japanese audio team; memory and zoo-recording paragraphs
sources.supports: Jungle demos joined; Beanland material borrowed/adapted; Gunn helped free audio memory; attempted zoo recordings did not enter game.
sources.limits: Wise qualifies the recollection about who supplied some voices; do not turn that into an exact vocal sample attribution.

sources.title: Double Trouble Ryan Hemsworth interviews Donkey Kong Country composer David Wise
sources.author: Ryan Hemsworth interviewing David Wise
sources.locator: Mood/instrument choices; Stickerbrush Symphony question; 2014 equipment question
sources.supports: Mood choices reflect collaboration, imagination and film/TV language; later methods and hardware belong to their stated period.
sources.limits: Stickerbrush/Bramble story is DKC2. Cubase and modern plug-in list describe 2014, not the 1994 DKC1 sessions.

sources.title: KORG WAVESTATION V2 product documentation
sources.author: KORG
sources.locator: A complete reproduction of the advanced vector synthesis system
sources.supports: Wave sequencing joins changing waveforms; vector synthesis controls modulation among oscillators.
sources.limits: Explains the synthesis family. Does not prove DKC1 used KORG hardware, factory patches or any particular sample; no purchase or installation recommendation.

sources.title: WAVESTATION Reference guide
sources.author: KORG
sources.locator: Original manual hosted by manufacturer; tool text extraction primarily exposed MIDI appendices
sources.supports: Manual reference for later detailed synthesis parameter research.
sources.limits: Wave-sequencing pages have not been visually reviewed in this pass; no parameter claim relies on them.

sources.title: A Rare Interview with Donkey Kong Country Composer Eveline Novakovic
sources.author: Jack Yarwood
sources.locator: Current link redirects to legacy article shell
sources.supports: Additional interview located for later recovery.
sources.limits: Article body unavailable in retrieved text; no factual claim imported from it. Date not resolved from the shell.
